summary: One-paragraph thesis for the second model.

Nike's FY2025 revenue fell to $46.3B from $51.4B the year before, and the stock has dropped from the $60-80 range into the high-$30s over the past year as the market re-rates the turnaround story. This model deliberately does not assume a margin recovery: revenue growth is held to a modest 3%/year and EBITDA margin flat at FY2025's depressed ~9.7% (operating income of $3.7B plus $775M of D&A, both from the 10-K). Even on that conservative, no-turnaround base case, the DCF implies about $43/share against an actual price near $37, suggesting the sell-off has priced in more pessimism than a flat-margin scenario justifies. The sensitivity table shows how much of that gap closes if WACC comes down a point or margins recover even partway toward Nike's historical ~12-13% range.

summary: Zomato (renamed Eternal Limited in 2024) grew revenue from ₹1,994 cr to ₹20,243 cr over the last five fiscal years, roughly a 59% CAGR, while profitability only turned durably positive recently (FY25 EBITDA margin of about 3-5% depending on whether you use the reported or the company's own adjusted figure). This model assumes growth decelerates from 30% to 15% over the next five years while EBITDA margin expands from 6% to 14% as the business scales, a maturing-platform path rather than a straight-line extension of either the current thin margin or the historical hypergrowth rate. Even with that expansion built in, the model implies roughly ₹30/share against an actual price near ₹322, the market pricing the stock at nearly 11 times this base case. That's the point of running the numbers, not a mistake to explain away: it means the market is pricing in materially faster growth, materially higher eventual margins, or both, than this base case assumes. Two inputs here are flagged estimates rather than clean filed figures, see the version note.
